parallel.requirements: Recognized the clean-room requirement and the need to reproduce zoxide CLI behavior from the bundled docs and executable: help/version text, add/query/remove/import/edit/init, environment variables, shell scripts, and buildable ./executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership and split black-box research into help/init, db mutation, and query behavior child scopes before building the replacement itself.
parallel.implementation: Implemented a Rust project with Cargo.toml, compile.sh, main logic, database/config modules, and generated init templates captured from observed shell outputs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent assembled the Rust sources, generated init assets, ran compile.sh, copied the release binary to ./executable, and delivered the artifact.
parallel.verification: Verification covered help/error output, mutation behavior, matching, import, edit, fzf behavior, init samples, and final build/version smoke checks.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The current official evaluator still failed 44 of 577 tests, so hidden edge cases or byte-level behavior remained incomplete despite broad coverage.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room task and probed zoxide CLI, database, import, query, edit, environment, and shell init behavior from the provided executable.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned all probing, implementation, fixes, build, and final verification without delegation or child-agent handoffs.
serial.implementation: Implemented a standalone Python executable in src/zoxide.py with compile.sh installing it to ./executable and creating a zoxide symlink.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run wrote the Python source and compile script, removed temporary probe helpers, ran compile.sh, and delivered the executable and symlink.
serial.verification: Verification used syntax checks, reference-vs-implementation probes, parser and fzf failure fixes, final version checks, query help, and sampled init output.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The current official evaluator failed 135 of 577 tests, and the final response explicitly left init output as structurally matched rather than exhaustive byte-for-byte.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel worked under the clean-room executable-and-documentation-only reverse-engineering task and targeted the full zoxide command surface.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had the identical prompt and also targeted the zoxide command surface from observation only.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement difference at the prompt level; differences came from implementation coverage and verification depth.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split research into help/init, database mutations, and query behavior while the parent retained implementation and final assembly ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a single trajectory with no spawn calls or child agent paths and owned all stages in one stream.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained concurrent research coverage; serial avoided handoffs but had less parallel information gathering.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child interfaces were research handoffs: help/init, database, and query findings returned to the parent as final messages.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent interfaces and accumulated findings locally before implementing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced handoffs but the handoffs were available and coherent; serial had no handoff risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built a Rust replacement and generated 216 init template files before implementing the runtime around them.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built a Python replacement in src/zoxide.py and installed it through compile.sh.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel emphasized static oracle-captured init fidelity and compiled Rust; serial used a larger dynamic Python implementation with sampled init generation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited/listed for children and received completed help, query, and database research results before final implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to retrieve, so its result lifecycle was ordinary sequential local state.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a completed, joined research lifecycle rather than an omitted or trapped child result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent wrote the actual Rust source tree and final build; child outputs were research-only and no contamination or shared-write problem was recorded.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a Python source tree, compile script, executable, and zoxide symlink from a single owner.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared information, not concurrent implementation ownership; serial had simpler state ownership.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran differential smoke checks against the release binary and reported broad representative coverage before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran syntax checks, reference comparisons, final build checks, version checks, query help, and sampled init output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified representative behavior, but parallel checked broader areas and had frozen init templates while serial left init byte fidelity as a known risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed without timeout after real child use and closed with a built artifact, though official evaluation still failed 44 tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed without timeout and closed with a built artifact, but official evaluation failed 135 tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither closure was caused by timeout or cancellation; parallel spent more tokens/requests and produced higher test coverage, while serial spent less and left more behavior unimplemented.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations make this a both_fail pair: parallel passed 533 of 577 tests and serial passed 442 of 577 tests, with solution_passed false for both. The score gap is best explained by ordinary strategy and coverage differences: parallel used child research and a Rust implementation with frozen init templates, while serial used a single Python implementation and acknowledged non-exhaustive init fidelity. No parallel coordination episode produced lost work, unjoined implementation, write collision, timeout, or an unsupported acceptance decision.
parallel_contributors: Useful child research returned concrete help/init, database, and query findings to the parent before implementation.
The parent froze observed init outputs into generated templates and performed broader representative verification.
serial_contributors: The serial run implemented in one Python file after sequential probing and had no child-agent handoffs.
The final serial response identified init behavior as structurally rather than exhaustively byte-for-byte matched.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel chose a Rust implementation with generated init templates; serial chose a Python implementation with generated shell text in code.
Both missed hidden evaluator behavior; these are implementation coverage defects rather than observable multi-agent coordination defects.
evaluator_effects: Official status.json evaluation, not stale aggregate interpretation, determines both_fail and the 533/577 versus 442/577 score gap.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, no discordant outcome and no retained concurrency pattern
